skills.name: Expand products of brackets and the special products

note.text:
To expand (x + a)(x + b), multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second, then collect like terms:
(x + a)(x + b) = x² + bx + ax + ab = x² + (a + b)x + ab.
Special products (learn them):
• (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²
• (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²
• (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²
A square is not the square of each term: (x + 3)² is x² + 6x + 9, not x² + 9.

sections.heading: Every term times every term
Squares of brackets
sections.text:
{'(x + ' + 3 + ')²'} means {'(x + ' + 3 + ')(x + ' + 3 + ')'}. Expand it like any product: x² + {mono(3, 'x')} + {mono(3, 'x')} + {9} = {poly([1, 'x²'], [6, 'x'], [9, ''])}.
The pattern is always: first squared, twice the product, last squared.
• (a + b)² = a² + {2}ab + b²
• (a − b)² = a² − {2}ab + b²
A common mistake is to write only x² + {9}: the middle term {mono(6, 'x')} is missing.

sections.heading: Sum times difference
sections.text:
When the brackets differ only in the sign, the middle terms cancel:
{'(x + ' + 5 + ')(x − ' + 5 + ')'} = x² − {mono(5, 'x')} + {mono(5, 'x')} − {25} = {poly([1, 'x²'], [-25, ''])}.
So (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b², the difference of two squares. You will use it backwards to factorise.

mistake.why: A square is the bracket times itself. The two middle products x × {4} and {4} × x give {mono(8, 'x')}.

cards.idea: Multiply every term of the first bracket by every term of the second: four products, then collect.
The square of a sum has a middle term: (a + b)² = a² + {2}ab + b².

misconceptions.explain: Squaring a bracket is not squaring each term: write it twice and expand; there is a middle term {mono(2 * a, 'x')}.
The middle term appears twice: {mono(a, 'x')} + {mono(a, 'x')} = {mono(2 * a, 'x')}.
The last term is {br(a)} × {br(a)} = {a * a}, not {2 * a}.

cards.idea: Sum times difference: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b². The middle terms cancel.

misconceptions.explain: {a} × {br(-a)} is negative: the last term is {-a * a}.
The x terms {mono(-a, 'x')} and {mono(a, 'x')} cancel: there is no middle term.
The last term is {a} × {br(-a)} = {-a * a}, a product, not {-2 * a}.
There are four products: x × {br(b)} and {a} × x make the middle term {mono(a + b, 'x')}.
The last term is a product: {a} × {br(b)} = {a * b}, not a sum.
The x terms are added: {mono(b, 'x')} + {mono(a, 'x')} = {mono(a + b, 'x')}.

solution: x × x = x²; x × {br(b)} + {a} × x gives {mono(a + b, 'x')}; {a} × {br(b)} = {a * b}.

misconceptions.explain: {p * q} is the coefficient of x² ({mono(p, 'x')} × {mono(q, 'x')}).
Multiply first: the x terms are {mono(p, 'x')} × {br(b)} and {a} × {mono(q, 'x')}.
